claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in its simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength but favorable plasticity and machinability.
The simple solid-solution state of CoCrFeNiTi is dominated by an FCC structure.
The absence of significant intermetallic phase formation and dominance of FCC structure govern the alloy's combination of low hardness and strength with favorable plasticity and machinability.
An FCC structure promotes dislocation mobility in CoCrFeNiTi.
An FCC structure suppresses brittle fracture in CoCrFeNiTi.
Simple FCC solid solutions have lower hardness and strength but higher ductility than similar alloys containing ordered intermetallics or complex multiphase microstructures.
Composition adjustment or heat treatment can promote ordering or precipitation of Ti-rich or Ni-Ti intermetallic phases in CoCrFeNiTi.
Intermetallics or complex phases impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion caused by intermetallics increases hardness and strength.
Intermetallic or complex phases reduce ductility.
CoCrFeNiTi samples with significant intermetallic phase content will have greater hardness and compressive strength than the FCC solid-solution baseline.
CoCrFeNiTi samples with significant intermetallic phase content will have lower plastic strain to failure and greater brittleness than the FCC solid-solution baseline.
The proposed mechanism is limited to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi compared in simple-solid-solution and multiphase or intermetallic states at 25 °C under compression or hardness loading.
